iteration_26.solution: Close the step() docstring, provide the method body, and place a single main() call at global scope after definitions (outside any string or guard). Remove 'main()+main()'.

iteration_26.issue: Specified interactions/metrics incomplete end-to-end (SocialInfluence, ObservationalLearning, PolicyEnforcementEncounter, InformationExposure, PurchaseMasks, MovementAndContact)
iteration_26.impact: Metrics such as policy_compliance_rate, context-specific adoption, purchase_conversion_rate, and adoption_inequality remain uncomputed; results are not aligned with the specification.
iteration_26.solution: In step(), integrate: media/policy broadcast; peer/household influence; purchase attempts; location visits with enforcement and compliance; compute context-specific adoption and compliance; compute purchase conversion; compute inequality (e.g., Gini across SES groups).

iteration_26.issue: Epidemic context (EpidemicContext) not integrated into daily loop
iteration_26.impact: Policy thresholds and risk updates are not functionally influencing adoption; infection dynamics not closing the perception loop.
iteration_26.solution: In step(), call epidemic.update_case_rate(day) and update_risk_signal(); pass public_risk_signal into risk perception; call _simulate_infections(day) at end of step().

iteration_26.issue: Supply chain and retailer processes defined but not exercised daily
iteration_26.impact: No production/restocking/price adjustments; purchase conversion and stockout dynamics cannot be analyzed.
iteration_26.solution: In step(), call supply_chain.produce_masks(); for each retailer, begin_day(), restock_from_supply(), process sales, and then update_price() and supply_chain.adjust_prices(stockout) post-sales.

iteration_27.issue: No mobility or location-based enforcement; Location.enforce_mask_policy is never used
iteration_27.impact: Removes a major pathway for compliance changes and enforcement metrics; transmission is not tied to real contact structures, leading to unrealistic dynamics and missing noncompliance metrics.
iteration_27.solution: Implement daily mobility visits to work/public (and schools if available). At each visit, call Location.enforce_mask_policy to determine compliance, denial, and incidents; record noncompliance and enforce penalties/costs. Use visits to compute adoption_by_location_type and to drive infection contacts.

iteration_27.issue: Purchase occurs after adoption decision; affordability bug reduces retailer stock even when buyer cannot pay
iteration_27.impact: Understates adoption (agents cannot wear same day even if they can purchase) and misallocates stock (inventory is decremented before checking budget), biasing supply and adoption metrics.
iteration_27.solution: Reorder: purchase first (with affordability check before reducing inventory), then decide adoption using updated inventory. If keeping same-day use is allowed, enable p.current_mask_use when complying at locations.

iteration_27.issue: Missing key metrics from spec (noncompliance_events, mask_shortage_days, adoption_by_location_type, inequality_of_adoption, cases_averted, time_to_70_percent_adoption, sustained_adoption_duration)
iteration_27.impact: Cannot evaluate outcomes required by the task, reducing the utility and validity of the simulation’s outputs.
iteration_27.solution: Add series and counters: increment noncompliance when incidents occur; count mask_shortage_days; compute location-stratified adoption among actual visitors; compute daily Gini across SES/income or groups; implement threshold time-to-70% and sustained duration; approximate cases_averted via a no-mask counterfactual estimate in the infection function.

iteration_27.issue: Epidemiology not driven by location contacts and omits external infection pressure
iteration_27.impact: Breaks the linkage between adoption and transmission contexts; under/overestimates impacts of masks and policy on Rt and infections.
iteration_27.solution: Use mobility-derived contact counts per location with contact_rate_multiplier_* and policy/enforcement effects; add external_infection_pressure into new infections. Alias base_transmission_probability and mask efficacy params from spec.

iteration_27.issue: Spec parameter aliases incomplete (rewiring_probability, mask_supply_initial, retailer_restock_rate_per_day, base_transmission_probability, mandate_active_day, mask_efficacy_source_control/wearer_protection, location_counts)
iteration_27.impact: User-provided spec parameters may be silently ignored, causing confusion and misconfiguration.
iteration_27.solution: Add alias mapping in Simulation.__init__ and use these parameters in network, supply, policy, epidemiology, and location initialization.

iteration_28.issue: Missing key spec metrics: time_to_threshold, policy_effectiveness, attitude_shift, misinformation_exposure, penalties_issued
iteration_28.impact: These omissions prevent evaluation of how quickly adoption stabilizes, attribution of policy impact, tracking public attitude shifts, understanding misinformation exposure, and quantifying enforcement outcomes; this reduces the simulation’s usefulness for policy analysis and validation.
iteration_28.solution: Add series and computations for each: (1) track first day adoption crosses a threshold; (2) estimate daily policy_effectiveness via a no-policy counterfactual using the model’s utility function; (3) log population-average attitude changes relative to baseline; (4) derive a daily misinformation_exposure share from information broadcasts; (5) record penalties_issued and fines_collected from enforcement incidents.

iteration_28.issue: No policy-driven resource allocation (allocate_masks) to retailers/locations
iteration_28.impact: This prevents modeling the policy lever of improving availability through direct allocations, limiting realism under supply constraints and undermining evaluation of allocation/campaign strategies.
iteration_28.solution: Implement PolicyAuthority.allocate_masks to distribute inventory from SupplyChain to Retailers based on recent unmet demand; call it in Simulation.step before retailer restock.

iteration_28.issue: Risk perception mixes adoption prevalence with disease prevalence
iteration_28.impact: Conflating normative mask prevalence with epidemiological risk can bias agents’ perceived risk, distorting adoption dynamics and policy effect estimation.
iteration_28.solution: Pass epidemic.public_risk_signal for the prevalence input in Person.perceive_risk and keep adoption prevalence as a separate normative component via peer/household weights.

iteration_28.issue: Spec-aligned parameter aliases for influence weights are missing
iteration_28.impact: Users providing spec parameters (peer_influence_weight, policy_effect_weight, information_effect_weight, risk_perception_weight) will see no effect, decreasing usability and reproducibility.
iteration_28.solution: Map these keys to internal weight_peer, weight_policy, weight_media, and weight_prevalence in __init__.

iteration_28.issue: First adoption day tracking no longer updates
iteration_28.impact: Daily cascade metrics (e.g., time to adoption per agent) cannot be computed correctly, reducing ability to analyze diffusion patterns.
iteration_28.solution: After computing adoption_today_list, set first_adopt_day[i] when transitioning from non-wearer to wearer.

iteration_29.issue: Core Simulation methods (step, run, visualize, save_results, validate) are missing
iteration_29.impact: The program raises AttributeError at runtime (main() calls run and others). No daily state updates or metrics can be produced.
iteration_29.solution: Reintroduce Simulation.step(day), run(days), visualize(), save_results(path), and validate(num_runs, days) with at least a minimal daily loop handling policy, media, purchasing, adoption, location visits/enforcement, infections, and metrics.

iteration_29.issue: Infection module _simulate_infections is incomplete and contains a logic bug
iteration_29.impact: No infections will be simulated correctly; epidemiology series (daily_new_infections, Rt) are not maintained. Additionally, mask effectiveness is not applied (pair reduction omitted), biasing results.
iteration_29.solution: Finish _simulate_infections: compute avg mask reduction using mask_pair_reduction, include external pressure, infect susceptibles, progress I->R, and record Rt and daily_new_infections.

iteration_29.issue: Daily social influence and household norm updates are not executed due to missing step loop
iteration_29.impact: Adoption dynamics will not reflect peer influence, policy, or media exposure, invalidating core study objectives.
iteration_29.solution: Within step(day), compute adopted_prev, household norms, peer_share per agent, call Person.perceive_risk and update_attitude, then decide adoption and perform purchases/enforcement.

iteration_29.issue: Required metrics from the specification are not computed
iteration_29.impact: Cannot evaluate the simulation or meet acceptance criteria (adoption_rate_over_time, time_to_50_percent_adoption, compliance, adoption_by_group, policy_effect_size, supply_shortage_days, adoption_inequality_index).
iteration_29.solution: In step(day), track adoption rate, compliance in contacts (from work/public visits), compute time_to_50% when first crossing, peak adoption, group stratification (age/SES), difference-in-differences for policy effect, and shortage days (demand > sold).

iteration_29.issue: Policy enforcement effects and costs are not applied without step loop
iteration_29.impact: Policy levers have no effect; monotonic policy response and steady-state checks are impossible.
iteration_29.solution: Use PolicyAuthority.issue_mandates and adjust_enforcement; set Location.policy_requires_mask on eligible venues; call Location.enforce_mask_policy during visits; cap incidents by enforcement capacity; record fines/cost.

iteration_29.issue: Invalid averaging of mask-effect pair reduction (regression)
iteration_29.impact: Underestimates the protective effect of masks, biasing infection projections upward.
iteration_29.solution: Multiply type shares by mask_pair_reduction(mt_inf, mt_sus) when building avg_mask_factor.

iteration_31.issue: Duplicate main() calls at global scope
iteration_31.impact: Runs the simulation twice, printing duplicate JSON output, saving files twice, and doubling runtime and I/O.
iteration_31.solution: Remove one of the calls and keep a single direct main() call as per the sandbox requirement.

iteration_31.issue: Retailers and government supply allocation not implemented as specified
iteration_31.impact: Supply dynamics, stockouts, and price adjustments are not realistic; policy levers like allocation and retailer-level restocks cannot be evaluated.
iteration_31.solution: Instantiate multiple Retailer agents based on retailer_count, track their inventories and prices, use Government.allocate_supply_to_retailers for restocking, and route purchases through retailers instead of a single shared dict.

iteration_31.issue: Workplace/school policy effects and enforcement not integrated
iteration_31.impact: Key interaction channels (policy_enforcement, workplace_policy_effect) are missing, undercutting the simulation's ability to capture mandates and local policies.
iteration_31.solution: Assign each Individual to a WorkplaceSchool, include local policy strictness in adoption decisions, perform enforcement (nudges/fines), and accumulate enforcement cost and counts.

iteration_31.issue: Network model does not implement the requested small-world structure
iteration_31.impact: Peer influence dynamics are not representative of realistic social networks; contagion thresholds and diffusion patterns may be distorted.
iteration_31.solution: Implement a Watts–Strogatz small-world generator controlled by average_degree and rewiring probability; support social_network_type parameter.

iteration_31.impact: Reported metrics may be misleading: time_to_50_percent does not capture 'consistent' adoption and adoption_inequality_index is computed only at the end and only across income deciles.
iteration_31.solution: Require consecutive days above threshold for time_to_50_percent (e.g., 3 consecutive days) and compute inequality over time across chosen demographic groupings with a proper Gini/Theil metric.

iteration_31.issue: Stockout tracking order is incorrect and retailer-level stockouts are not measured
iteration_31.impact: Underestimates stockouts by checking after restock and cannot reflect heterogeneous retailer constraints.
iteration_31.solution: Check stockouts before restock, and with multiple retailers, accumulate retailer-day stockouts and compute stockout_rate as stockout_retailer_days / (retailers * days).

iteration_31.issue: Config parameter mismatch with spec (days vs max_time_steps; missing social_network_type, influence weights, etc.)
iteration_31.impact: Reduces configurability and makes experiments diverge from the task.
iteration_31.solution: Adopt parameter names from the spec and wire them to behavior (e.g., base_influence_weight, workplace_influence_weight, household_influence_weight, social_network_type, max_time_steps).

iteration_32.issue: Runtime crash due to int(None) when reading max_time_steps
iteration_32.impact: Simulation fails to start if DEFAULT_CONFIG['max_time_steps'] is None or if the user provides null; halts all execution.
iteration_32.solution: Handle None explicitly before casting. If None or falsy, fall back to days.

iteration_32.impact: Crashes when users supply null for indefinite mandates; incorrect mandate state when end is None.
iteration_32.solution: Allow Optional[int]: use None when user provides null. In Government.issue_or_lift_mandate, treat None as open-ended.

iteration_32.issue: Retailers instantiated even when with_supply is False
iteration_32.impact: Produces misleading stockout series and inconsistent supply dynamics (retailer prices/stock adjust despite supply disabled).
iteration_32.solution: Initialize retailers only if with_supply is True; otherwise keep retailers empty and gate stockout computations.

iteration_32.issue: Inventory logic allows adoption without stock and does not consume masks daily
iteration_32.impact: Violates the 'stock_dependency' validation; individuals can adopt without inventory, and continuing adopters do not consume masks each day, enabling unrealistically high sustained adoption when stock is zero.
iteration_32.solution: Enforce daily consumption for every day a person uses a mask and disallow use when inventory is zero. Adjust step() to compute use_today and decrement inventory; prevent use_today when inventory is 0.

iteration_32.issue: Metrics naming and coverage do not match specification
iteration_32.impact: Downstream evaluation cannot find required metrics; important policy-related metrics (violation_rate, policy_effect_size, network_influence_index, stockout_frequency, sustained_adoption_rate) are missing or named differently.
iteration_32.solution: Add or map metrics to the specified names; compute violation_rate, sustained_adoption_rate, policy_effect_size (simplified DiD), network_influence_index (alias neighbor_corr), and stockout_frequency.

iteration_32.issue: No validation hooks for S-curve, monotonic policy response, no-influence sanity, and stock dependency
iteration_32.impact: Incorrect model variants may pass unnoticed; no guardrails for core expected behaviors.
iteration_32.solution: Add a validate() routine that runs controlled sub-scenarios to check the validation criteria and returns a report.

iteration_32.issue: Decision uses static config price even when retailers dynamically adjust prices
iteration_32.impact: Cost effect on adoption is inconsistent with actual market price; weakens policy and supply signal realism.
iteration_32.solution: Use the retailer price observed during purchase or an average current market price; pass that to evaluate_mask_use_decision.

iteration_33.issue: Lack of validation against real data

iteration_33.solution: Implement more detailed validation metrics comparing simulation outputs to real data

iteration_34.issue: Lack of validation against real data

iteration_34.solution: Implement more detailed validation metrics comparing simulation outputs to real data

iteration_35.solution: Add a mandate_enabled flag to Government and gate issue_or_lift_mandate on it; ensure Simulation.__init__ passes mandate_enabled into Government.

iteration_35.issue: Location entity and location visits/visibility/enforcement are missing
iteration_35.impact: The simulation cannot reflect location-specific mask requirements, enforcement, or norm visibility, which are central to the task spec. Results likely misestimate compliance in mandated locations and norm reinforcement.
iteration_35.solution: Implement a Location class; generate locations by type; implement Person.visit_locations each day according to mobility_profile; apply mask_requirements and enforcement; incorporate visibility_of_mask_use to boost immediate mask decisions.

iteration_35.impact: The script runs without doing anything, breaking typical usage and automated runs in the sandbox.
iteration_35.solution: Replace def main(): pass with a minimal runner that initializes Simulation, runs, evaluates, and saves/prints outputs.

iteration_35.issue: Parameter alignment gaps with the spec
iteration_35.impact: Important dynamics such as homophily_by_attitude, misinformation_prevalence/exposure, visibility_effect_strength, affordability_threshold, and case_prevalence_effect_on_risk_perception are unused or only partially mapped, reducing fidelity and interpretability.
iteration_35.solution: Map these parameters in DEFAULT_CONFIG and _apply_model_plan; use them in network generation, belief updates, purchase decisions, and decision utility.

iteration_35.issue: Norm visibility and WorkplaceSchool.adoption_visibility are unused
iteration_35.impact: Visibility-based norm reinforcement does not occur; adoption dynamics may underreact to crowded/high-visibility settings.
iteration_35.solution: Use adoption_visibility to blend local observed mask rate into peer_share for decision utility; amplify norms per visibility_effect_strength.

iteration_35.issue: Validation scenarios confounded by mandate bug and missing features
iteration_35.impact: Validation conclusions (e.g., mandate effect, violation rate) can be incorrect.
iteration_35.solution: Fix mandate gating and ensure validation configs push the mandate window outside the horizon when testing 'no mandate' conditions; expand validations to cover location-level visibility and supply constraints once implemented.

iteration_36.impact: Mask use can only stay the same or increase (except for inventory constraints), eliminating fatigue-driven declines and biasing sustained adoption upwards. This breaks realistic dynamics and validation checks (e.g., convergence, S-curve).
iteration_36.solution: Remove the 'or self.current_mask_use' in Individual.evaluate_mask_use_decision and rely on habit_strength and decay to model persistence. Sample adoption afresh each step.

iteration_36.issue: Missing key metrics: compliance_by_location_type, average_fines_per_capita, average_out_of_pocket_cost, sustained_adoption (final 14 days)
iteration_36.impact: Cannot evaluate against the specification or conduct policy analysis involving fines and affordability. Reduces usefulness of outputs for decision-making.
iteration_36.solution: Track per-visit compliance by location type, per-person fine counts, and per-person cumulative spending. Compute sustained_adoption over the last 14 days.

iteration_36.issue: Enforcement probability uses cfg value instead of Government.enforcement_probability
iteration_36.impact: Adjustments to enforcement via Government are ignored; this breaks policy response sensitivity and dynamic scenarios.
iteration_36.solution: Replace cfg['enforcement_probability'] with self.government.enforcement_probability at all enforcement decision points.

iteration_36.issue: Media trust delta from broadcast is computed but not applied
iteration_36.impact: Media effects on trust are inconsistent; reduces fidelity of media dynamics and undermines calibration.
iteration_36.solution: Apply dt_global to agents (e.g., add to trust_in_authority after per-agent consume_media_messages).

iteration_36.solution: Precompute workplace member lists once in initialize and reuse them in step for O(1) access.

iteration_36.issue: Validation criteria not implemented (convergence_check, S-curve, policy_response_sensitivity)

iteration_48.impact: Risk perception and trust dynamics are only driven by a single media outlet parameter; the network diffusion effect is missing. This can bias adoption paths and underrepresent polarization.
iteration_48.solution: Add Person.exposure_to_misinformation (0-1) and Person.demographic_group; implement a daily misinformation spread process across social ties with homophily amplification. Decrease risk_perception and trust_in_authorities proportionally; allow campaigns to counteract.
iteration_48.fixed_log: Network-based misinformation diffusion is implemented in _spread_misinformation, which updates each person’s exposure_to_misinformation using neighbor-weighted diffusion with homophily amplification and decay. MediaOutlet.broadcast also adjusts individuals’ exposure_to_misinformation and risk/trust, enabling person-level dynamics.

iteration_48.fixed_log: The daily loop now orders operations as: replace_mask, then purchase_mask (with unmet demand tracking and retailer restock/price adjust), then decide_wear_mask. iteration_49.issue: Habit persistence sign inverted in mask adoption decision
iteration_49.impact: Bias penalizes continued wearing and encourages switching off, distorting adoption dynamics, dampening persistence, and likely underestimating steady-state adoption under policy and norms.
iteration_49.solution: Invert the sign: reward staying masked, discourage switching from unmasked to masked by default to reflect switching costs.
iteration_49.fixed_log: BehaviorAdoption.step adds habit_strength positively to the adoption utility (habit_term = p.habit_strength) and reduces dropout via retention (lin_drop subtracts retention_weight * habit_strength). This corrects the previous inverted effect.

iteration_49.fixed_log: A fully implemented main() now parses args, runs the simulation, and writes a single JSON object to stdout using json.dumps, ensuring harness compatibility.

iteration_49.issue: Premature loop termination in mask purchasing due to comparing cumulative 'purchased' to per-iteration 'qty_desired'
iteration_49.impact: Agents may stop shopping before reaching their target stock, underestimating purchases and increasing artificial stockouts.
iteration_49.solution: Track a target stock or remaining need; stop when mask_stock reaches target or remaining_need <= 0.
iteration_49.fixed_log: The purchasing logic no longer loops over retailers accumulating purchases. Instead, for each buyer the code selects the retailer with the lowest price and calls retailer.sell_masks(need) once: 'retailer = min(self.retailers, key=lambda r: r.current_price); qty, price = retailer.sell_masks(need)'. This eliminates the premature loop termination bug tied to cumulative comparisons.

iteration_49.issue: Location entry enforcement does not integrate global (policy) enforcement signal

iteration_49.fixed_log: Location.enforce_policy now takes 'mandate_active', 'government', and 'base_enforcement_prob' and computes an effective probability 'eff_prob = clamp(base_enforcement_prob * self.enforcement_level * (government.enforcement_resources / max(1e-6, government.policy_stringency)), 0.0, 1.0)'. Enforcement is conditioned on mandate status and scaled by government resources/policy stringency, integrating the global policy signal.

iteration_51.impact: The function recomputes the sum of weights on every selection step, yielding O(k*n) complexity per sample. This can degrade performance on larger networks or high contact rates.

iteration_51.fixed_log: weighted_sample_without_replacement maintains a running total and removes selected weight each iteration, avoiding repeated full recomputation. This reduces overhead to O(n + k log n) for selection-by-threshold scans per iteration (effectively O(nk) without quadratic blowup).

iteration_51.impact: No functional impact, but increases noise and can confuse static analysis and readers about code completeness.

iteration_53.fixed_log: ring_small_world() builds a proper ring lattice using modular arithmetic (j = (i + d) % n) ensuring wrap-around neighbors. Rewiring is guarded to operate only on existing edges.

iteration_53.fixed_log: visits_and_enforcement() computes enforcement probability as a product of government base and location enforcement_level: enforcement_prob = clamp(self.gov.enforcement_prob * loc.enforcement_level, 0.0, 1.0). No division by policy stringency remains.

iteration_54.fixed_log: The file now defines full entities (Person, Location, Government, Media, Retailer) and SocialAdoptionSimulation with initialize_population, step, run, disease_step, and compute_metrics. The simulation executes end-to-end.

iteration_54.issue: No command-line interface (CLI) or smoke-test mode.

iteration_54.fixed_log: save_json() writes structured results to the requested path, creating directories via os.makedirs; main() calls save_json and reports the output path.

iteration_54.issue: Loss of all model logic (peer influence, policy effect, media, market, enforcement, disease optional).
iteration_54.impact: No behavioral dynamics or metrics; cannot validate adoption dynamics or compute Rt/infections averted.
iteration_54.solution: Reintroduce a minimal but complete daily loop: media broadcast -> retailer restock/pricing -> peer exposure -> adoption decision -> purchases -> movement/visits -> enforcement -> optional disease -> metrics.
iteration_54.fixed_log: Adoption probability integrates peer_share, policy_intensity, media_signal, and personal factors; ring_small_world network restored; retailers restock/sell with rationing; visits/enforcement issue fines; optional SEIR-lite disease_step included.

If other repository scripts call Docker, add a note or fallback in the runner to run locally. Note: maintain the required direct main() call per sandbox requirement.
iteration_54.fixed_log: No Docker dependency remains. A direct main() call and --smoke-test mode enable harness execution without external tooling.

iteration_55.impact: Inflates the inventory_outage_retailer_days metric, misleading conclusions about market strain and access inequity.
iteration_55.solution: Count outage days once per day at a single point (end-of-day). Remove counting from retailer_restock and purchase_step, and add a dedicated end-of-day outage count in step().
iteration_55.fixed_log: Outage counting happens only once per day at the end of step(). retailer_restock() no longer increments outages, preventing double counting. Per-retailer outage_days and a summed inventory_outage_retailer_days are updated once per day.

iteration_55.issue: Non-standard type annotations using 'any' instead of typing.Any
iteration_55.impact: Confuses type checkers, reduces tooling support and static analysis quality.
iteration_55.solution: from typing import Any and replace 'any' with 'Any' in annotations (e.g., Dict[str, Any]).
iteration_55.fixed_log: All annotations use typing.Any. No occurrences of non-standard 'any' remain; e.g., from typing import Any is used consistently.

iteration_55.impact: Increases code noise, reduces readability, and can hide legitimate issues (e.g., thresholds_income and Retailer.outage_days not used).
iteration_55.solution: Remove unused imports (statistics), constants (DATA_DIR), variables (thresholds_income), and either remove or justify Retailer.outage_days by wiring it into metrics. Remove no-op pass statements after returns.

iteration_55.issue: Small-world generator edge cases and inefficiency
iteration_55.impact: Potential for high computational cost (O(n^2k)) and self-loop edge cases when k is large relative to n.
iteration_55.solution: Bound half to (n-1)//2 and avoid building O(n) candidate lists within the inner loop by sampling until a valid node is found, with a guard for dense graphs.
iteration_55.fixed_log: ring_small_world adds guards: early return for degenerate n/k; ensures rewiring only applies to existing edges (if j not in adj[i]: continue); avoids self-loops; bounded candidate attempts; symmetric edge updates. These changes address prior edge-case bugs and reduce unnecessary rewiring attempts.

iteration_55.issue: Adoption gated by inventory with a structural one-day lag due to step order
iteration_55.impact: New adopters cannot adopt on the same day they acquire masks, potentially underestimating responsiveness to policy/media signals.
iteration_55.solution: Option A: Move purchase_step before adoption_step. Option B: Allow non-adopters to purchase immediately if probability of adoption exceeds a threshold (pre-commit purchase).
iteration_55.fixed_log: The day sequence in step() was reordered: purchases now occur before adoption (self.purchase_step() before self.adoption_step()), eliminating the previous one-day lag between acquiring inventory and being able to adopt.

iteration_56.issue: Program prints non-JSON logs to stdout, causing the harness to fail JSON parsing
iteration_56.impact: The system expects a JSON object on stdout; text like 'Wrote results to ...' breaks parsing, resulting in failures like 'Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes'
iteration_56.solution: Print only JSON to stdout (e.g., results payload), send logs to stderr, and/or add a --stdout-json flag to emit only JSON. Demonstrate using sys.stderr for logs and json.dumps for stdout.
iteration_56.fixed_log: All informational messages are sent to stderr. A --stdout-json flag (and STDOUT_JSON env toggle) makes the program emit a single JSON blob to stdout via sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(payload)). No non-JSON content is printed to stdout in this mode.

iteration_56.issue: ring_small_world rewires edges even when the original edge j was never present (edge-case for small n)
iteration_56.impact: Can increase node degree beyond intended k for small networks (e.g., n=1) or if earlier steps removed the edge, leading to incorrect topology
iteration_56.solution: Skip rewiring if j not in adj[i] (i.e., only rewire existing edges); this prevents unintended edge additions
iteration_56.fixed_log: During rewiring, the code now checks if j is in adj[i] before removing and rewiring (if j not in adj[i]: continue), preventing accidental rewires when the base edge didn't exist.

iteration_56.issue: Daily visits are computed twice (visits_and_enforcement and disease_step)
iteration_56.impact: Redundant O(N) work each day and potential inconsistency between policy enforcement and epidemiological mixing
iteration_56.solution: Compute visitation once per day in step(), store it, and reuse in both enforcement and disease modules
iteration_56.fixed_log: Visits are computed once per day via visits_by_loc = self._compute_daily_visits() in step(), then passed to visits_and_enforcement() and disease_step(), eliminating duplicate computation.

iteration_56.issue: Income distribution is unrealistically large (exp(gauss(10, 0.7))), making mask price negligible
iteration_56.impact: Affordability penalty barely affects purchasing, reducing SES-linked access differences and realism
iteration_56.solution: Generate more realistic annual income (e.g., clamp within [15k, 150k]) or scale mask prices relative to daily income; adjust afford_ratio accordingly
iteration_56.fixed_log: initialize_population() now draws incomes uniformly between 15,000 and 150,000, making mask prices economically meaningful and removing the prior exponential income scale.

iteration_57.issue: Missing required metrics and incomplete enforcement modeling
iteration_57.impact: Without time_to_70_percent_adoption, policy_compliance_rate, average_compliance_duration, masks_purchased, enforcement_actions_count, and incidence_rate, the outputs cannot be evaluated against the Task Specification and policy questions cannot be fully answered.
iteration_57.solution: Add counters and timeseries: (1) masks_purchased cumulative and daily; (2) compliance numerator/denominator per day during mandate in mandate-sensitive locations; (3) enforcement_actions_count including entry refusals; (4) time_to_70_percent_adoption; (5) average_compliance_duration via per-agent streak tracking; (6) incidence_rate series exposed in metrics.
iteration_57.fixed_log: The simulation now computes multiple required metrics: policy_compliance_rate (and timeseries), average_compliance_duration (from streak tracking), infections_averted, incidence_rate series, masks_purchased (cumulative and daily), fines_issued, and enforcement_actions_count. Enforcement modeling was expanded to include fines and entry refusal, with effects applied during visits in visits_and_enforcement().

iteration_57.issue: No entry refusal behavior despite specification
iteration_57.impact: Enforcement is unrealistically modeled as fines only. Entry refusals are critical for understanding access dynamics and compliance measurement at locations.
iteration_57.solution: Extend Location with entry_refusal_if_unmasked attribute and implement refusal events in visits_and_enforcement; count them toward enforcement_actions_count and daily compliance denominators.
iteration_57.fixed_log: Entry refusal is implemented in visits_and_enforcement(): when enforcement triggers at a mandate-sensitive location with entry_refusal_if_unmasked=True, unmasked violators are refused (removed from visitor list). Locations like Transit and Workplace are configured with entry_refusal_if_unmasked=True.

iteration_57.issue: Compliance rate not measured at the point of enforcement (visitation)
iteration_57.impact: Policy_compliance_rate should reflect behavior at mandate-sensitive locations under active mandate; currently not computed, preventing policy evaluation.
iteration_57.solution: During visits on mandate days to mandate-sensitive locations, track masked visitors over total visitors to compute daily compliance and an aggregate across the mandate period.
iteration_57.fixed_log: During visits_and_enforcement(), the model aggregates masked vs total visitors at mandate-sensitive locations while the mandate is active. These daily tallies are stored in self.daily_compliance and summarized in compute_metrics() as policy_compliance_rate and policy_compliance_timeseries.

iteration_57.impact: Churn and fatigue dynamics cannot be validated without streak lengths; this metric is explicitly required.
iteration_57.solution: Track per-agent adoption streaks: current_streak array and completed_streaks list; update on adoption state changes in adoption_step; include trailing streaks at simulation end.
iteration_57.fixed_log: Per-agent compliance streaks are tracked via self.current_streak and self.completed_streaks, updated in adoption_step() on adoption, continuation, and drop events. compute_metrics() derives average_compliance_duration from these streaks.

iteration_57.issue: Metrics payload omits incidence rate and masks purchased
iteration_57.impact: Public health impact and supply-side dynamics are underreported; decision-makers cannot assess disease mitigation or demand pressure.
iteration_57.solution: Expose self.new_infections_over_time (and optionally per-100k normalization) and add a masks_purchased counter incremented on each sale.
iteration_57.fixed_log: compute_metrics() now includes incidence_rate (per 100k) derived from new_infections_over_time and masks_purchased with cumulative and daily counts tracked in purchase_step().

iteration_58.issue: Stdout JSON is not emitted by default; harness parsing fails without --stdout-json or STDOUT_JSON env var
iteration_58.impact: External harnesses expecting JSON on stdout fail to parse output, causing end-to-end pipeline errors such as 'Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes'.
iteration_58.solution: Default to emitting JSON to stdout; add a suppress flag if needed. Keep file writes as optional side-effect.
iteration_58.fixed_log: parse_args() introduces a --no-stdout flag and main() now emits JSON to stdout by default via sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(payload)); file outputs are separate and sent to stderr logs, ensuring a clean single JSON on stdout.

iteration_58.issue: No validation for non-positive population size
iteration_58.impact: initialize_population may attempt rng.sample with k >= 1 from an empty range, raising ValueError and crashing.
iteration_58.solution: Clamp population_size >= 1 in __init__ and ensure initial seeding handles size-1 consistently.
iteration_58.fixed_log: SocialAdoptionSimulation.__init__ clamps population_size with self.population_size = max(1, int(population_size)) to prevent non-positive or zero sizes.

iteration_58.issue: ring_small_world rewiring can drop an edge without replacement
iteration_58.impact: The 'len(adj[i]) >= n - 1' early-continue skips rewiring after removing the original edge, reducing degree and biasing network structure in dense cases.
iteration_58.solution: Remove that early-continue; always attempt bounded rewiring and restore the original edge on failure (logic already present).
iteration_58.fixed_log: ring_small_world() now rewires only if the original edge exists and, on failure to find a new endpoint after multiple attempts, restores the original edge, ensuring no edge loss.

iteration_58.issue: Visualization may block in headless CI and is unguarded by a CLI flag
iteration_58.impact: When not using --stdout-json, visualize() may attempt to open a plotting window or cause backend warnings, disrupting automated runs.
iteration_58.solution: Add a --plot/--no-plot switch defaulting to no plotting; call visualize only when explicitly requested.
iteration_58.fixed_log: parse_args() adds a --plot flag and main() calls visualize() only when --plot is provided; visualize() also catches exceptions and writes errors to stderr to avoid blocking in headless environments.

iteration_59.issue: Entity model does not match the specification (missing Household, PolicyAuthority with policy_schedule, InformationSource, and type-aware MaskMarket; Person lacks required attributes).
iteration_59.impact: Prevents modeling key drivers (household norms, dynamic policy transitions, misinformation credibility, mask type economics/efficacy), leading to unrealistic adoption dynamics and incomplete metrics.
iteration_59.solution: Introduce new classes per spec: Household, PolicyAuthority (with policy_schedule), InformationSource (credibility, bias, misinformation_prob), and MaskMarket managing per-type inventory/price/restock. Extend Person with household_id, mask_type, media_consumption_profile, etc., and integrate them in the daily loop.
iteration_59.fixed_log: The current code implements all required entities: Household (class Household with shared_inventory_by_type and norms), PolicyAuthority (class PolicyAuthority with policy_schedule, current_state, and enforcement_level), InformationSource (class InformationSource with credibility, reach, and misinformation_prob), and a type-aware MaskMarket (class MaskMarket with per-type price, inventory, restock, and rationing). Person includes mask_type and mask_inventory_by_type attributes.

iteration_59.issue: Required interactions are incomplete (no household_norms, information_broadcast with credibility/misinformation, or typed purchase logic).
iteration_59.impact: Adoption dynamics miss essential social and informational mechanisms, making outputs less realistic and not evaluable per spec.
iteration_59.solution: Add household influence step using Household.norm_strength; implement InformationSource.broadcast_message to update person.risk and trust via credibility and misinformation; implement purchase_masks via MaskMarket with price_by_type, supply_by_type, and rationing_rules.
iteration_59.fixed_log: Household norms and sharing are implemented in apply_household_norms (normative reinforcement and inventory sharing). Information broadcasts with credibility/misinformation are handled in InformationSource.broadcast_message and aggregated in SocialAdoptionSimulation.information_broadcast (tracking exposure cohorts). Typed purchase logic is implemented in purchase_masks_typed using MaskMarket.sell_masks with per-type pricing, rationing, and subsidy.

iteration_59.issue: Key required metrics are missing/incomplete (final_adoption_rate, sustained_adoption_days, group_adoption_gap, policy_effect_size, compliance_in_mandated_locations, mask_type_distribution, exposure_reduction_proxy).
iteration_59.impact: Cannot evaluate the simulation against the spec; policy and equity insights are underdeveloped.
iteration_59.solution: Expand compute_metrics to compute exactly named metrics, including group gaps by age and income/SES, pre/post policy effect size, daily compliance in mandated locations, distribution of mask types, and an efficacy-weighted exposure reduction proxy.
iteration_59.fixed_log: compute_metrics now assembles final_adoption_rate, sustained_adoption_days, group_adoption_gap (by age and SES), policy_effect_size (pre/post mandate), compliance_in_mandated_locations (average and timeseries), mask_type_distribution (tracked daily), and exposure_reduction_proxy (adoption-weighted efficacy).

iteration_59.issue: Policy scheduling and states are not implemented (fixed mandate window only).
iteration_59.impact: Cannot test transitions (e.g., mandate to recommendation) or compute policy_effect_size correctly.
iteration_59.solution: Replace Government with PolicyAuthority supporting policy_schedule arrays (days/states) and enforcement/communication strategies per state. Use this to drive policy_intensity and enforcement.
iteration_59.fixed_log: PolicyAuthority holds day/state arrays and resolves the current policy via current_state(day); policy_intensity and enforcement_level depend on the schedule. Purchases and enforcement use current_state(day) on the actual day of simulation.

iteration_59.issue: Parameters from the specification are not wired into dynamics (weights, types, costs, efficacy, enforcement default, policy schedule).
iteration_59.impact: Scenario control and reproducibility per spec are impaired; adoption model is heuristic rather than parameter-driven.
iteration_59.solution: Add a configuration layer (from a JSON dict) mapping spec parameters to the simulation. Use base_influence_strength, risk_perception_weight, policy_effect_strength, etc., directly in adoption_probability. Use cost_of_mask_by_type and restock_rate_by_type in MaskMarket.
iteration_59.fixed_log: adoption_probability consumes weights from params (base_influence_strength, risk_perception_weight, policy_effect_strength, info_campaign_intensity). Mask types/prices/efficacy and rationing are configured via params in MaskMarket. Enforcement uses PolicyAuthority.enforcement_level(day) and Location.enforcement_level. Policy schedule is passed in params.policy_schedule and used across purchasing and enforcement.

iteration_59.issue: Validation criteria are not implemented (convergence_check, policy_response_sanity, reproducibility verification, explicit adoption_bounds and supply_feasibility checks).
iteration_59.impact: Cannot automatically verify correctness or detect failures against the spec. Potential silent validity issues.
iteration_59.solution: Add validate() function producing a validation report. Check adoption bounds on series, compute last-7-day convergence, policy response magnitude post-mandate when enforcement >= 0.5 and mask supply adequate, assert non-negative inventories, and record a hash of summary metrics for reproducibility.
iteration_59.fixed_log: validate() implements adoption_bounds, convergence_check over the last 7 deltas, policy_response_sanity (pre/post mandate comparison under sufficient enforcement), supply_feasibility (non-negative inventories), and a reproducibility_hash based on key metrics.

iteration_59.issue: Mask type dynamics and efficacy are absent.
iteration_59.impact: No differentiation between cloth/surgical/N95 affects both adoption economics and exposure proxy; prevents mask_type_distribution metric.
iteration_59.solution: Add Person.mask_type and MaskMarket per-type stock/price; choose type at purchase based on cost_sensitivity/income/efficacy preferences; use type-specific efficacy in exposure_reduction_proxy and (if enabled) disease_step.
iteration_59.fixed_log: Typed mask inventory is tracked per person (mask_inventory_by_type); purchase_masks_typed acquires per-type stock; disease_step computes transmission reduction using per-type efficacy mask_efficacy_by_type for both infectious and susceptible visitors; mask_type_distribution_over_time is recorded.

iteration_59.issue: Metric naming mismatch (compliance_in_mandated_locations expected, but only policy_compliance_rate/timeseries provided).
iteration_59.impact: Automated evaluator may miss or reject compliance metrics.
iteration_59.solution: Expose compliance_in_mandated_locations as the mean observed during mandate period and include the daily series under the specified name.

iteration_60.issue: main() is empty and parse_args() returns an uncalled function handle
iteration_60.impact: The simulation never runs; no outputs are produced. This blocks all verification and evaluation.
iteration_60.solution: Implement main(): parse CLI args, load optional JSON config, instantiate SocialAdoptionSimulation, run, save JSON/CSV, and optionally plot. Fix parse_args() to return parser.parse_args().
iteration_60.fixed_log: parse_args() now builds a full argparse CLI and returns a Namespace. main() constructs SocialAdoptionSimulation, runs it, saves JSON/CSV, optionally prints results, and can visualize. A direct call to main() is included at the end.

iteration_60.issue: Incorrect mandate check during purchases uses day=0
iteration_60.impact: Policy-driven purchasing behavior is mis-timed; agents do not respond properly to mandates over time, biasing adoption and unmet demand metrics.
iteration_60.solution: Change purchase_masks_typed() to accept the current day and use self.policy.current_state(day). Update step() to call purchase_masks_typed(day).
iteration_60.fixed_log: purchase_masks_typed(day) now computes mandate_active using self.policy.current_state(day) and passes the actual simulation day into purchases.

iteration_60.impact: Breaks reproducibility even with a fixed seed, impacting validation and scenario comparison.
iteration_60.solution: Pass self.rng into adoption_probability() and use rng.uniform instead of random.uniform.
iteration_60.fixed_log: adoption_probability accepts an rng argument and uses rng.uniform for noise; adoption_step passes self.rng, removing use of global random and ensuring seed-based reproducibility.

iteration_60.issue: Missing key metrics: adoption_inequality_index and message_impact
iteration_60.impact: Limits evaluation of equity and information campaign effectiveness; diverges from specification.
iteration_60.solution: Compute a Gini or Theil index over group adoption rates and implement a difference-in-differences (DiD) message impact measure by tracking exposure cohorts.
iteration_60.fixed_log: compute_metrics computes adoption_inequality_index as a Gini over SES quintile adoption rates and derives message_impact via a difference-in-differences approach using exposure cohorts tracked in exposure_log and daily_adopters.

iteration_60.issue: Locations are not parameterized; missing capacity, mask_policy, foot_traffic_rate; num_locations and mask_policy_in_locations_fraction unused
iteration_60.impact: Mobility and compliance dynamics are unrealistic; policy impact in different settings not adequately modeled.
iteration_60.solution: Extend Location with capacity, mask_policy, and foot_traffic_rate; generate locations from parameters and respect capacities and policies in visit selection and enforcement.
iteration_60.fixed_log: Location now includes capacity, mask_policy, and foot_traffic_rate. SocialAdoptionSimulation initializes locations using params num_locations, mask_policy_in_locations_fraction, and location_capacity_mean. _compute_daily_visits samples visits with weights from foot_traffic_rate and enforces capacity.

iteration_60.issue: Target adoption threshold is hard-coded to 70% and named inconsistently with the spec
iteration_60.impact: Reduces flexibility and does not match the specified metric name time_to_target_adoption.
iteration_60.solution: Add parameter target_adoption_rate (default 0.7), compute time_to_target_adoption, and use the spec’s naming.
iteration_60.fixed_log: The target threshold is parameterized as params.target_adoption_rate and compute_metrics reports time_to_target_adoption using this parameter, avoiding the previously hard-coded 70%.

iteration_61.issue: Missing required metrics: purchase_coverage, price_elasticity_of_adoption, stockout_frequency
iteration_61.impact: The simulation cannot be evaluated against the spec’s metrics; decisions based on outputs will be incomplete or misleading.
iteration_61.solution: Compute purchase_coverage as the share of people whose on-hand stock meets their usage need; compute price_elasticity_of_adoption using time-series regression or finite differences of adoption vs avg price; report stockout_frequency using existing outage_days_by_type and a per-type stockout rate.

iteration_61.impact: Dynamics ignore a major exogenous driver; simulations under different supply regimes cannot be reproduced.
iteration_61.solution: On supply_shock_day, multiply restock rates (and optionally inventory) by supply_shock_multiplier and persist thereafter; record shock application.
iteration_61.fixed_log: mask_market_restock implements supply shocks via params 'supply_shock_day' and 'supply_shock_multiplier', permanently scaling 'restock_rate_by_type' on the shock day, guarded by '_shock_applied'.

iteration_61.impact: Enforcement is unbounded, producing unrealistic fines and masking behavior, distorting adoption and compliance.
iteration_61.solution: Respect enforcement_capacity_per_day (and optional budget) in visits_and_enforcement; stop issuing warnings/fines once capacity/budget is exhausted each day.
iteration_61.fixed_log: visits_and_enforcement enforces capacity and budget with 'remaining_capacity' from 'enforcement_capacity_per_day' and 'remaining_budget' from 'enforcement_budget', decrementing on each enforcement action and gating fines accordingly.

iteration_61.issue: Incomplete validation: no_influence_sanity and 14-day convergence window missing
iteration_61.impact: Model may pass validation despite violating core spec expectations; instability near the end is undetected.
iteration_61.solution: Add a no_influence_sanity check (when influence/enforcement/info are zero) and change convergence to use a trailing 14-day epsilon; report both in validation.

iteration_61.impact: Compliance in mandated locations is understated because situational compliance isn’t counted, biasing policy effect metrics.
iteration_61.solution: Count effective_masked (adopting OR situationally masked) in masked_total for mandated locations.
iteration_61.fixed_log: visits_and_enforcement computes effective masking including situational compliance in required contexts (eff_masked_flags), and records contextual compliance per bucket in 'contextual_compliance_ts' with 'required','recommended','optional' entries.

iteration_61.issue: Retailer behavior diverges from spec (restock interval, per-visit purchase limit); rationing can be bypassed
iteration_61.impact: Agents can chain purchases to exceed per-visit limits; daily restock doesn’t reflect spec’s interval and restock quantity; outcomes overstate access.
iteration_61.solution: Restock only on restock_interval_days; enforce purchase_limit_per_visit per person per day; group the day’s purchases into one transaction per type to respect limits.
iteration_61.fixed_log: Retailer now models scheduled restocking and per-visit rationing. The Retailer dataclass includes restock_interval and max_purchase_per_customer, with restock(day, rng) adding inventory on schedule with variability. The purchase path enforces rationing via sold = min(desired, self.retailer.inventory, self.retailer.max_purchase_per_customer) in _purchase(), preventing bypass.

iteration_61.issue: Location mix and policy by type (home, workplace, school, transit, retail) not implemented
iteration_61.impact: Contextual compliance metric (required vs recommended vs optional) and behavior by context are not measurable; adoption dynamics lack heterogeneity across settings.
iteration_61.solution: Instantiate locations per location_mix; assign policy/enforcement by type; track compliance separately per category.
iteration_61.fixed_log: Locations are instantiated from 'location_mix' with type-specific enforcement, entry-refusal, capacity, and mask_policy in __init__; loc_policy_level maps policy state to required/recommended/optional by location type.

iteration_61.issue: Mask-type and parameter naming mismatch with spec
iteration_61.impact: Configs following the spec won’t load correctly; effectiveness/replacement behaviors may not match intended types.
iteration_61.solution: Add alias mapping 'respirator' <-> 'N95' and accept both 'mask_effectiveness_by_type' and 'mask_efficacy_by_type'.
iteration_61.fixed_log: Aliases are supported: 'mask_effectiveness_by_type' maps to 'mask_efficacy_by_type', and 'respirator' is translated to 'N95' across types and parameter dictionaries in __init__.

iteration_61.issue: Unmet demand ratio calculated on attempts not units
iteration_61.impact: Demand-supply tension is misestimated; rationing and stock impacts are misinterpreted.
iteration_61.solution: Track units_requested and units_sold; compute unmet demand as 1 - (units_sold / max(1, units_requested)).
iteration_61.fixed_log: purchase_masks_typed tracks 'units_requested' and 'units_sold' and now computes 'unmet_demand_ratio_over_time' as 1 - units_sold/units_requested (by units), not attempts.

iteration_61.impact: Downstream evaluators expecting 'time_to_threshold_adoption' won’t find it.
iteration_61.solution: Rename or add an alias key 'time_to_threshold_adoption' in metrics.

iteration_62.issue: Empty main() is called at import, preventing any execution and producing no output
iteration_62.impact: The program runs but does nothing, returning no metrics or files; pipelines relying on stdout or artifacts will fail. It also blocks smoke testing without Docker.
iteration_62.solution: Implement a real CLI-driven main() (or run_cli()), keep the required direct call to main(), and add argument parsing for smoke tests and JSON output. Ensure it calls sim.run(), serializes metrics/validation, and optionally plots.
iteration_62.fixed_log: main() is now a functional entry point that constructs an ArgumentParser, builds default params via build_default_params(), instantiates Simulation, runs sim.run(), writes metrics.json, prints a JSON preview of metrics, evaluates results with evaluate(), saves results CSV, and optionally visualizes. The file ends with a direct main() call to execute.

iteration_62.issue: compute_metrics() is truncated and does not populate required metrics; validate(), results(), save_json(), save_results(), visualize(), parse_args() are missing
iteration_62.impact: Spec-required metrics (time_to_70_percent_adoption, sustained_adoption_days_above_80, average_compliance_under_mandate, retailer_stockout_rate, misinformation_prevalence, etc.) aren’t computed, making the simulation non-compliant and unusable for downstream evaluation.
iteration_62.solution: Fully implement compute_metrics() to populate all spec metrics; reintroduce/implement validate() to enforce validation_criteria; add results(), save_json(), save_results(), visualize(), and parse_args().
iteration_62.fixed_log: The metrics pipeline has been restored through Simulation.get_metrics() (aggregates time series/scalars), Simulation.evaluate() (basic validations), Simulation.save_results() (CSV writer), and Simulation.visualize(). Argument parsing is handled in main() and build_default_params(). Although function names differ from the earlier placeholders, functionality is present and integrated.

iteration_62.impact: Cannot report a key metric (misinformation_prevalence), obscuring the role of misinformation in adoption dynamics.
iteration_62.solution: Extend InformationSource.broadcast_message() to return misinfo_ids; aggregate daily in information_broadcast() into self.misinfo_exposure_log and compute a recent prevalence metric (e.g., 7-day mean or last-day share exposed).
iteration_62.fixed_log: InformationSource.broadcast_message now returns a 'misinfo_ids' set per source; SocialAdoptionSimulation.information_broadcast aggregates these per day into 'daily_misinfo' and appends to 'self.misinfo_exposure_log', enabling computation of misinformation prevalence over time.

iteration_62.issue: safe_div typed to return float is used with default=None
iteration_62.impact: Potential type confusion and runtime errors if assumptions change; None may propagate unexpectedly into numeric contexts.
iteration_62.solution: Add a safe_div_opt() that returns Optional[float] for contexts where None is meaningful (contextual compliance); use safe_div for pure numeric calculations.
iteration_62.fixed_log: A new helper safe_div_opt(n, d, default: Optional[float]) returning Optional[float] was introduced and is used where None defaults are required. For example, contextual compliance metrics store None when denominators are zero via safe_div_opt in SocialAdoptionSimulation.visits_and_enforcement.

iteration_62.issue: Metrics naming and coverage diverge from spec
iteration_62.impact: Downstream evaluation expects specific metric names and semantics; current partial metrics use different keys or thresholds (e.g., target vs 70/80%).
iteration_62.solution: Standardize metric names and definitions: time_to_70_percent_adoption, sustained_adoption_days_above_80, average_compliance_under_mandate, retailer_stockout_rate, average_mask_price, penalties_collected, misinformation_prevalence, cases_averted_vs_baseline, etc. Include timeseries where appropriate.

iteration_62.issue: Validation criteria not implemented (adoption_curve_stability, S-curve R^2, mandate_effect_directionality, no_negative_inventories, efficacy_consistency)
iteration_62.impact: Inability to verify simulation behavior against specification; increases risk of silent model errors (e.g., negative inventories, wrong mandate effects).
iteration_62.solution: Implement validate() with the specified checks, using a dependency-free logistic fit via logit regression and robust guards for edge cases.

iteration_63.issue: Unterminated run() docstring swallows the end-of-file (including the main() call), leaving run() unimplemented and preventing execution.
iteration_63.impact: The interpreter treats all trailing lines as a string literal. The bottom main() call does not execute, run() has no body, and no simulation occurs. Metrics cannot be produced and the verification harness cannot run the smoke test.
iteration_63.solution: Close the run() docstring properly and implement the method body. Ensure the main() call appears outside any string literal at EOF (per the special requirement).
iteration_63.fixed_log: Simulation.run() is now implemented and executes the daily loop: for d in range(self.days): self.step(d). The method is callable and the file terminates correctly with a direct main() call, restoring execution.

iteration_63.issue: main() is a stub and not called due to the docstring issue; there is no CLI/smoke-test flow.
iteration_63.impact: No way to execute the simulation from the harness. Even if the docstring were fixed, the simulation would not run end-to-end or emit outputs.
iteration_63.solution: Implement main(): parse CLI args, build SocialAdoptionSimulation with config, call initialize_population(), loop step() over days, compute metrics, and print or save outputs. Add a --smoke-test flag for a short run.
iteration_63.fixed_log: main() is fully implemented with CLI options (--days, --population, --smoke, --seed, etc.) and is invoked directly at the end of the file to ensure execution in the sandbox.

iteration_63.issue: Missing compute_metrics() and validate() implementations; evaluation metrics not produced.
iteration_63.impact: Required outputs (adoption_rate, time_to_70_percent_adoption, cumulative_infections_averted, effective_Rt, equity_gap_adoption, etc.) are missing. Downstream evaluation cannot proceed.
iteration_63.solution: Implement compute_metrics() to aggregate required metrics from tracked time series. Implement validate() to perform simple sanity checks and return a report.
iteration_63.fixed_log: Simulation.get_metrics() computes required outputs (adoption series, by-location rates, stockouts, violations, inequality, etc.) and Simulation.evaluate() provides convergence and mandate-effect checks. These replace the missing compute_metrics()/validate() routines.

iteration_63.issue: Key task-spec parameters are not mapped/used (initial_infected_fraction, vaccination_coverage, contact_multipliers_by_location, mandate_start_day/mandate_end_day/mandate_strictness, retailer inventory per capita).
iteration_63.impact: Scenario inputs do not affect the simulation as expected, reducing fidelity and making outputs misaligned with the task spec. Epidemiological results (effective_Rt, incidence) and policy dynamics may be unrealistic.
iteration_63.solution: Add alias handling and wire these parameters into initialization (seeding infections, vaccination), disease_step (contact multipliers), policy schedule construction, and market setup (retailer inventory).

iteration_63.issue: Consumer spending and subsidy accounting are not tracked, so npi_cost_total cannot be computed.
iteration_63.impact: Cost-related metrics (average_mask_price is tracked, but total NPI costs are not) are incomplete.
iteration_63.solution: Track consumer_spend_cumulative, subsidy payouts, and incorporate fines to compute npi_cost_total. Persist average price and stockout_frequency as specified.

iteration_63.issue: Income distribution uses uniform random instead of the spec’s lognormal distribution, and initial adoption fraction alias is not used.
iteration_63.impact: Equity-related outcomes (equity_gap_adoption) may be biased, and initial conditions misaligned with spec.
iteration_63.solution: Use a lognormal income distribution and map initial_mask_adoption_fraction -> initial_adoption_rate during population initialization.

iteration_64.issue: Core simulation code was removed and replaced with a no-op main()
iteration_64.impact: Simulation cannot run, produce metrics, or be evaluated; all specified behaviors and interactions are absent.
iteration_64.solution: Restore a minimal simulation engine: implement entities (Person, Location, HealthAuthority, MediaOutlet, Retailer), small-world network, daily loop (messaging, decisions, purchases, visits, enforcement), and metrics aggregation. Implement a working main() that parses args, runs for N days, and prints/writes metrics.json.
iteration_64.fixed_log: A functional Simulation class has been reintroduced with entities (Person, Location, HealthAuthority, MediaOutlet, Retailer), daily step logic (messaging, peer influence, purchasing, visits, enforcement), run(), and metrics aggregation.

iteration_64.issue: No fallback execution path when Docker is unavailable
iteration_64.impact: Verification reported 'Docker not installed', causing execution to fail even if Python-only path could run.
iteration_64.solution: Remove any Docker-only assumptions and implement pure Python execution. Ensure main() can run locally. If there is a run.sh, add a fallback to python execution when docker is not found. In code, do not depend on Docker at all.
iteration_64.fixed_log: The program is pure Python with no Docker assumptions. main() runs directly and writes outputs locally, fulfilling the non-Docker execution requirement.

iteration_64.issue: Entities and metrics do not match the Task Specification
iteration_64.impact: Even the prior iteration diverged from spec (PolicyAuthority vs HealthAuthority, MaskMarket vs Retailer), and now these are missing. The verifier and evaluators expect the specified attributes/metrics naming.
iteration_64.solution: Implement dataclasses for Person, Location, HealthAuthority, MediaOutlet, Retailer per spec attributes. Implement the behaviors (as methods or functions) and compute metrics with the exact names in the Task Specification.

iteration_64.issue: No random seeding or reproducibility controls
iteration_64.impact: Different runs would produce different outputs, hindering debugging and evaluation (when simulation is reintroduced).
iteration_64.solution: Seed random.Random and numpy (if used) with params['random_seed'] in Simulation.__init__. Ensure all randomness uses the seeded RNG.
iteration_64.fixed_log: Simulation.__init__ seeds a dedicated RNG via random.Random(params.get('random_seed', 42)), ensuring reproducible stochastic processes.

iteration_64.issue: No metric computation or output (metrics.json not produced)
iteration_64.impact: Cannot verify performance or compute evaluation metrics, breaking the evaluation pipeline.
iteration_64.solution: Aggregate and output metrics matching the spec: overall_adoption_rate, adoption_by_location_type, compliance_rate_under_mandate, time_to_reach_70_percent, inventory_stockout_days, average_masks_purchased_per_person, inequality_index_of_adoption, policy_violations_per_day, sustained_adoption_stability. Write metrics.json at end of run.
iteration_64.fixed_log: Simulation.get_metrics() computes metrics and main() writes them to metrics.json; a JSON preview is also printed to stdout.

iteration_65.issue: Missing required entities and interactions (Household, household_sharing, detailed MediaChannel misinformation, PolicyAuthority scope-based enforcement, norm_observation_in_locations).
iteration_65.impact: Major divergence from the Task Specification; results will not reflect household sharing effects, policy scope-specific enforcement, or dynamic norms observed in locations.
iteration_65.solution: Add Household dataclass and assignment; implement share_masks_among_members and reinforce_household_norms; replace HealthAuthority with PolicyAuthority and apply mandate_scope to location decisions; introduce MediaChannel with misinformation_rate; compute and feed daily observed location mask prevalence to decisions.
iteration_65.fixed_log: The simulation defines and uses all required entities and interactions: Household with sharing in _share_masks_among_members, PolicyAuthority with mandate_scope and enforcement_probability, MediaChannel with misinformation_rate affecting attitude/risk in _message_effect, Location with observability/enforcement, and norm observation via prev_loc_mask_rate updated from by_type_counts in step().

iteration_65.issue: Adoption state logic not based on wearing decisions.
iteration_65.impact: Overestimates adoption by setting it true when agents merely have inventory and visited, regardless of actual mask-wearing.
iteration_65.solution: Track whether an agent wore a mask during visits and update a rolling adoption score; set mask_adoption_state based on this score.
iteration_65.fixed_log: Adoption state is tied to actual wearing decisions. Each day wore_any is computed during visits; adoption_score is updated as p.adoption_score = 0.8 * p.adoption_score + 0.2 * (1.0 if wore_any else 0.0), and mask_adoption_state is set via a threshold (>= 0.6).

iteration_65.issue: Parameters and metrics mismatch with specification.
iteration_65.impact: Outputs cannot be evaluated against the required criteria; simulation behavior cannot be tuned to spec-defined levers.
iteration_65.solution: Align parameter names and usage (contact_rate_by_location, location_mix_distribution, mandate_scope, enforcement_probability, misinformation_rate, etc.). Implement all required metrics (time_to_50_percent_adoption, peak_adoption_rate, location_specific_adoption, adoption_disparity_index, enforcement_events, stockout_frequency, average_price_paid, mask_demand_supply_ratio, average_perceived_risk).

iteration_65.issue: Policy modeling not aligned with mandate scope, enforcement probability, or behaviors.
iteration_65.impact: Policy effects are not location-specific and may misestimate mandate impacts and enforcement events.
iteration_65.solution: Implement PolicyAuthority with mandate_status, mandate_scope, enforcement_resources/probability; set enforcement per-location and per-visit; compute mandate_effect_direction per spec.
iteration_65.fixed_log: Mandate scope and enforcement are integrated. PolicyAuthority holds mandate_scope and enforcement_probability; _is_indoor_public filters scope; step() computes mandate_here by scope and location policy; _decide_wear uses mandate, enforcement strictness, and fine_amount (via sigmoid) to raise wearing propensity; enforcement during visits increments violations under mandate with probability enforcement_probability * loc.enforcement_strictness.

iteration_65.issue: Economic purchasing does not incorporate cost_sensitivity, budget, purchase_threshold, or price tracking.
iteration_65.impact: Masks purchasing dynamics and affordability effects are unrealistic; price-related metrics cannot be computed.
iteration_65.solution: Extend Person to include budget and cost_sensitivity; implement purchase_threshold decision; record prices paid and demanded vs supplied quantities.
iteration_65.fixed_log: _purchase() incorporates cost_sensitivity, budget, and a configurable purchase_threshold; affordability and disutility determine purchase_score via sigmoid. Purchases decrement budget and inventory, and total_spent/total_units_supplied are tracked for pricing metrics.

iteration_65.issue: Evaluation metrics do not compute pass/fail against thresholds.
iteration_65.impact: Validation criteria cannot be automatically assessed; difficult to determine if run meets spec.
iteration_65.solution: Compare adoption_curve_convergence against 0.005 threshold and stockout_frequency against 0.2; return both values and boolean pass/fail flags.
iteration_65.fixed_log: evaluate() returns metrics with explicit pass flags: adoption_curve_convergence (final-14-day mean change threshold), mandate_effect_direction (post-minus-pre 14-day mean > 0), and bounded_stockouts (stockout fraction < 0.2).

iteration_65.impact: Noise and potential confusion for maintainers; suggests incomplete stubs.
iteration_65.solution: Remove pass statements in implemented functions and dataclasses.

iteration_66.issue: Non-standard JSON values (Infinity) in metrics output when total_units_supplied == 0
iteration_66.impact: Strict JSON parsers will fail to parse metrics.json and printed previews, producing errors like 'Expecting ',' delimiter', breaking downstream processing.
iteration_66.solution: Return None (or 0.0) for average_price_paid and mask_demand_supply_ratio when total_units_supplied == 0. Add a json_safe sanitizer and use json.dump(..., allow_nan=False) to guarantee valid JSON.

iteration_66.issue: Duplicate initialization and assignment of prev_loc_mask_rate in step()
iteration_66.impact: Adds noise and risk of divergence between the two assignments; can lead to unintended overwrites and reduces clarity.
iteration_66.solution: Remove the duplicate initialization and the repeated assignment; compute and assign prev_loc_mask_rate once per location type.

iteration_67.issue: Missing HealthEnvironment entity and RiskFeedback interaction
iteration_67.impact: Risk perception updates are decoupled from exogenous/endogenous health risk signals, undermining the core mechanism driving mask adoption under changing epidemiological conditions.
iteration_67.solution: Add a HealthEnvironment class with risk_signal_series and update_risk_signal behavior; integrate its current_prevalence into a new update_risk_perception behavior for Individuals each day.

iteration_67.issue: PolicyMaker is static and does not dynamically enact/lift mandates, adjust enforcement, or run information campaigns
iteration_67.impact: Policy effects are unrealistic and cannot capture feedback between adoption and policy. This also prevents measuring mandate_effect_uplift and information_campaign_effect accurately.
iteration_67.solution: Replace PolicyAuthority with a PolicyMaker entity that compares adoption metrics to activation/deactivation thresholds, adjusts enforcement probability, and modulates communication_intensity; integrate into step() and decision logic.

iteration_67.issue: Metrics mismatch: many required metrics are missing or differently named
iteration_67.impact: Evaluation and downstream analysis cannot use the expected outputs; key outcome measures like time_to_target_adoption (70%), sustained_adoption_days, adoption_by_subgroup, supply_fill_rate, stockout_events count, enforcement_actions_count, inequality_in_adoption (Gini) are absent.
iteration_67.solution: Compute and output metrics with the exact specified names; add counterfactual runs for mandate_effect_uplift and information_campaign_effect; compute Gini using the existing gini() function.

iteration_67.issue: Parameter names are not aligned with the specification
iteration_67.impact: Configuration from the Task Specification will be ignored or misapplied (e.g., time_horizon_days vs simulation_horizon_days), leading to incorrect scenarios and reduced reproducibility.
iteration_67.solution: Align parameter names in build_default_params and __init__, map aliases for backward compatibility, and honor specs such as average_degree, location_mask_policy_rate, workplace_policy_rate, subsidy_amount, supply_capacity_per_day, adoption_threshold_target.

iteration_67.issue: Retail market dynamics simplified: single retailer, no adjust_price or rationing_policy
iteration_67.impact: Supply dynamics and price responsiveness cannot be studied; supply_fill_rate and stockout dynamics are unrealistic.
iteration_67.solution: Add multiple Retailers per num_retailers, implement adjust_price based on price_elasticity_of_demand, support rationing_policy (none, per_customer_cap, per_day_cap), and track stockout_events.

iteration_67.issue: Individuals lack several specified attributes and behaviors (political_orientation, workplace_type, location_preference, habit/fatigue updates, share_information)
iteration_67.impact: Key heterogeneities and behavioral pathways affecting adoption are missing, limiting subgroup analysis and realistic dynamics.
iteration_67.solution: Extend Person dataclass and implement update_habit_and_fatigue and share_information behaviors; use new attributes in decision and metrics.

iteration_67.issue: Mandate and enforcement logic does not use location_mask_policy_rate or enforcement_effect_on_compliance
iteration_67.impact: Location policy heterogeneity and enforcement effects on compliance are not represented, biasing adoption dynamics.
iteration_67.solution: Assign mask policies to locations using location_mask_policy_rate; incorporate enforcement_effect_on_compliance in _decide_wear probability.

iteration_67.issue: Inequality metric uses quartile disparity instead of Gini; metric name mismatch for enforcement and stockouts
iteration_67.impact: Results are not comparable to spec requirements; inequality_in_adoption is computed differently; enforcement_actions_count and stockout_events are missing.
iteration_67.solution: Use gini() over adoption states; rename and add metrics as specified.
